task: discrete visual vocabulary from frozen FetalCLIP patch features (IMPACT, 20413 frames, 12 of 24 layers)

flat_single_codebook.note: first run crashed on json int64 AFTER training and lost outputs; rerun with fix saved model+code maps

findings: Depth-factorised vocabulary reconstructs better than flat (0.298 vs 0.366) and no codebook collapses (all fully used).
Depth-specific content dominates: shared-only recon 0.830 (near the ~1.0 no-recon baseline) vs 0.298 full -> the depth-invariant part carries little; the per-depth deviations carry most.

GA is DIFFUSE, not depth-localised: max |code-freq vs GA| rho is 0.10-0.15 in EVERY vocabulary (shared and all three private). The weak GA structure is a property of FetalCLIP patch features, not of the flat architecture.
caveats: RECON COMPARISON NOT BIT-MATCHED: flat = 8 bits/patch (1-of-256); factorised = 25 bits/patch (1-of-128 + 3x 1-of-64). Part of the 0.366->0.298 improvement is extra discrete capacity, not factorisation per se. A bit-matched control is required before claiming factorisation itself wins.

SHARED-ONLY metric partly built in: shared = MEAN across groups while each group is the reconstruction target, so if groups differ the mean is inherently a poor predictor. The direction is real; the +0.53 effect size is inflated by the mean+residual construction.
EMA codebook + dead-code reinit were required: an earlier image-level VQ (gradient codebook, full-batch) collapsed to 9/32-12/64 codes with near-zero GA ladder and was NOT reported as a finding.
next_control: bit-matched factorised vs flat (e.g. shared K=32 + private K=8x3 ~= 14 bits vs flat K=16384 impractical -> match downward: flat K=64 (6 bits) vs shared K=16 + private K=4x3 (~10 bits), or equalise by shrinking private codebooks until total bits == flat bits)

code_combination_GA_probe.protocol: per-image code-frequency histograms; GroupKFold-by-fetus; greedy forward selection INSIDE training folds only (nested, inner 3-fold), r measured on held-out fetuses; GA-shuffle null through the identical pipeline

reference_ceiling.note: The VQ codes are FetalCLIP-derived, so the valid same-cohort ceiling is the FetalCLIP IMPACT clock r=0.469 (L18/24). An earlier version of this file wrongly used 0.435, which is the USF-MAE value from the same 4-encoder run. The 0.906 is a DIFFERENT cohort (30257 clinical frames, GA 6.2-41.6wk) and is not a ceiling for these IMPACT frames (GA 26-40.6wk).

findings: The discrete vocabulary RETAINS most of the continuous clock: all 320 code frequencies give held-out r=0.385 vs the FetalCLIP full-embedding clock r=0.469 on the same IMPACT frames (82% of the ceiling). Quantisation to 320 visual words costs little GA information.

GA lives in the DEPTH-SHARED vocabulary: shared alone r=0.374 (128 codes) nearly equals ALL 320 (0.385), while each depth-private vocabulary is much weaker (shallow 0.134, mid 0.230, deep 0.164). Adding all three private blocks to shared buys only +0.011.

NO compact subset carries GA: nested forward selection rises slowly and monotonically (1 code 0.125 -> 20 codes 0.271) and at k=20 is still well below all-320 (0.385). GA is genuinely DISTRIBUTED across the vocabulary, not concentrated in a few words.

Selection is stable and non-random: the same features are chosen in 5/5 folds (6 of the top 8 are SHARED codes), and the GA-shuffle null is flat (all-codes r=-0.006, combo k=20 r=0.002) - so the selection procedure itself produces nothing by chance.
code_combination_GA_probe.corrects_earlier_framing: An earlier reading called GA 'diffuse' based on single-code Spearman rho of 0.10-0.15. That was a UNIVARIATE statement only. Multivariately the codes carry GA well (0.385 of a 0.469 FetalCLIP ceiling (82%)). The correct statement is: GA is distributed across many codes (no single code or small subset carries it) and concentrated in the depth-SHARED vocabulary rather than any single depth.
caveats: IMPACT-only, GA 26-40.6wk (narrow). The distributed/shared conclusions are established on this window; the wide-GA clinical set was not run through this probe.

Selection used an in-fold |corr| pre-screen capped at 64 candidates, so the k-subset curve is a greedy path, not the global optimum over all C(320,k) subsets - it bounds, not proves, subset performance.

Shared vs private are not equal-capacity (128 vs 64 codes each); part of shared's advantage is its larger vocabulary. The shared-vs-ALL comparison (0.374 vs 0.385) is the capacity-fair statement, not shared-vs-one-private.
corrections: Ceiling corrected 0.435 -> 0.469: 0.435 was USF-MAE, not FetalCLIP. The codes are FetalCLIP-derived, so retained fraction is 82.1% (not the 88.5% previously stated).

baselines_UNIT_MATCHED.note: Topics are fitted/scored per FETUS, so 0.615 is the valid ceiling for them. 0.385 is the only value comparable to the FRAME-level FetalCLIP full-embedding clock r=0.469 (0.385/0.469 = 82%). An earlier run compared fetus-level topic r to the frame-level 0.385 and to 0.469 - both invalid.

findings: UNIT-MATCHED verdict: topics do NOT beat the raw code histogram. The per-fetus histogram ceiling is r=0.615; the best topic latent (FA, R=32) reaches 0.609 = 99% of it, and every rank below 32 is at 60-78%. Factorising the histogram into topics COSTS GA information at low rank and only recovers it by using enough factors to approximate the full histogram.

The apparent 'topics beat the histogram' reading in the first run was a UNIT ARTEFACT: fetus-level topic r (0.424/0.458) was compared to the FRAME-level histogram r (0.385). Per-fetus mean pooling suppresses noise and mechanically raises r; the correct fetus-level baseline is 0.615.

GA r is NOT monotone in rank (0.368/0.380/0.379/0.408/0.433/0.577) but rises steeply at R=32 while plateauing 4-8. R=32 is the largest rank tried and its NMF needed 5226 iterations - the gain looks like capacity approaching the full 320-d histogram, not a discovered low-dimensional maturation structure.

Both nulls pass at every rank: matched-capacity shuffled-histogram NMF gives NEGATIVE r (-0.03 to -0.11) and GA-shuffle gives ~0.00 (max |0.029|). The structure that IS there is real, not capacity artefact.

The latent is a CONTINUUM: silhouette k=2 is 0.13-0.30 at every rank, and does not improve with rank. Replicates the continuum finding of every prior family in this project (GBTM dip-unimodal, HDBSCAN all-noise, unsupervised beta-TCVAE overlay).

PLANE dominates and grows with rank: max topic plane eta2 rises 0.49 -> 0.78 as rank increases. Extra factors are largely spent encoding imaging plane, not maturation - i.e. the vocabulary's leading structure is acquisition geometry.

Topic composition is dominated by SHARED codes (top-5 loadings are mostly shared#*), consistent with the earlier finding that GA lives in the depth-shared vocabulary (shared-alone r=0.374 vs all-320 0.385 at frame level).

Two topics are reproducible across every rank: a positive-GA topic led by shared#49/#109/#95/#17 (mono +0.31..+0.39) and a negative-GA topic led by shared#7/#5/#56 (mono -0.21..-0.36). These are the closest thing to interpretable maturation axes here, but |mono| never exceeds 0.39.
caveats: OUTCOME READ-OFFS STILL NOT RUN: impact_outcomes.csv is absent on the HPC at both searched paths (exists=False). No SGA/LGA/birth-percentile anchor has been evaluated on this latent.
NMF converged at every rank under the raised 8000-iteration cap, but R=32 needed 5226 iterations - near the practical limit; its loadings are the least stable of the set.

IMPACT-only, GA 26.0-39.3wk. A 'maturation vocabulary' cannot be properly tested in a 13-week late window; the clinical cohort (30257 frames, 544 fetuses, GA 6.2-41.6wk, SD 6.92) is the correct substrate and has NOT been run.

plane_prop is kNN-propagated and was audited unreliable on the clinical set (3 of 6 wrong at conf=1.00), so the plane eta2 magnitudes carry label noise (which would DEFLATE, not inflate, measured plane structure).
topic_latent_bag_of_visual_words.verdict: NEGATIVE for the topic latent as an improvement: bag-of-visual-words factorisation does not organise GA better than the raw code histogram it is built from, and the extra factors mostly encode imaging plane. The codes remain a usable scan representation (82% of the frame-level FetalCLIP clock), but NMF topics are not the way to add value on top of them.

shared_private_factorisation_RETRACTED.what_it_retracts: The depth-factorised result previously reported here and to the user -- FULL recon 0.298 vs SHARED-ONLY 0.830, framed as 'private adds +0.53, depth-specific content dominates' -- is WITHDRAWN as a finding. shared was defined as the arithmetic MEAN over E=3 depth groups, and the mean of E independent streams carries exactly 1/E of the variance regardless of whether anything is truly shared. The observed shared fraction (0.334) equals the analytic floor (0.333) and sits inside the 200-permutation shuffle band [0.333,0.334], excess +0.000. The +0.53 'private gain' was an arithmetic identity of the mean+residual construction, not evidence about depth-specific content.
shared_private_factorisation_RETRACTED.also_applies_to: The cross-encoder version of the same design (E=4 encoders, floor 0.250) must NOT be relaunched on this construction -- it would reproduce the same identity at 0.250. The run was stopped.
shared_private_factorisation_RETRACTED.verdict_label_bug: The script's first-run label said 'WEAK -- above the band' because obs beat p95 by <0.001 of rounding. A bare '>p95' gate is too weak when the band is this tight; fixed to require excess >= 0.02 minimum effect size as well as clearing the band. Correct label for this run: NO shared structure.
shared_private_factorisation_RETRACTED.what_survives: Nothing about shared-vs-private. The codebook results that do NOT depend on this construction are unaffected: flat K=256 VQ recon 0.366 with 256/256 codes alive; code histogram retains held-out GA r=0.385 at frame level (82% of the FetalCLIP 0.469 ceiling) and 0.615 per-fetus; GA distributed not compact; 95% of GA r survives regressing plane out; NMF topics null; continuum not clusters.
